name: JEE Advanced
conductingBody: Joint Admission Board (JAB) – one of seven zonal IITs by rotation
approxCandidates: Top ≈2.5 lakh JEE Main qualifiers eligible; ≈1.8–1.9 lakh register and appear
eligibility: Among top ≈2.5 lakh in JEE Main (category-wise); max 2 attempts in consecutive years; born on/after 1 Oct 2002 (5-yr relaxation SC/ST/PwD); Class 12 in 2026 or 2027

notification.summary: The 2026 exam was held by IIT Roorkee on 17 May 2026. As of 10 Oct 2026 the JAB had not announced the organising IIT or dates for JEE Advanced 2027 (IIT Delhi is widely expected by rotation but unconfirmed); the exam is expected in the second or third week of May 2027.

importantDates.date: Late Apr – early May 2027 (expected, after JEE Main Session 2 result)

pattern.notes: Two compulsory 3-hour papers on the same day; the structure changes every year. A recent Paper 1 (2025) had per subject: 4 single-correct MCQs (+3/−1), 3 one-or-more-correct MCQs (+4 with partial marking/−2), 6 non-negative integer questions (+4/0) and 4 matching-list MCQs (+3/−1); some 2026 analyses report 17 questions per subject. This mock simulates the single-correct MCQ format (+3/−1) only.

trendAnalysis.summary: JEE Advanced remains concept-integrating and lengthy; Mathematics and Physics have alternated as the toughest subject (Physics reported toughest in 2026, Mathematics in 2024). Calculus, probability, matrices and vectors/3D dominate Mathematics; mechanics (rotation, fluids), electrostatics/magnetism and modern physics dominate Physics. Chemistry is the most scoring section but physical chemistry numericals and mechanism-based organic questions have grown, while inorganic stays NCERT-anchored (coordination, p-block). Integer-type and matching questions keep guessing low; cut-offs have been around 25–30% of total marks for the common rank list.

pyqBlueprint.method: Compiled from the officially released JEE Advanced Paper 1 and Paper 2 question papers and answer keys (IIT Madras 2024, IIT Kanpur 2025, 2026 cycle) as summarised in public analyses (Careers360, Physics Wallah, coaching institute paper reviews), which web search confirmed for chapter emphasis (modern physics, optics, E&M, mechanics; thermodynamics, bonding, coordination; calculus, matrices, probability, vectors/3D). Full paper PDFs could not be fetched, so recurring concept + format + trap patterns were written from the drafter's own knowledge of these papers. MSQ/integer/matching items are represented by their underlying concept recast as single-correct MCQs.

archetypes.pattern: Screw gauge / vernier calliper reading with positive or negative zero error — corrected measurement; trap is the sign of the correction
Dimensional analysis of combinations of fundamental constants (h, c, G, e, ε₀) or error propagation in derived formulae
Projectile or relative-motion condition (velocity perpendicular to initial velocity, river/boat crossing, collision in air)
Two-block system with friction between blocks on a smooth floor: maximum force for no slipping, accelerations of each block
Elastic/inelastic collisions and successive bounces: energy fractions, coefficient of restitution, total distance
Spinning/sliding ring, disc or sphere placed on a rough surface: final rolling speed via angular momentum about the contact point
Rolling on an incline: accelerations, speeds, minimum friction coefficient for pure rolling for different bodies
Orbital speed, escape speed, period ratios and energy changes for satellites
Hydrostatics in accelerating frames (lift, cart): capillary rise, fraction submerged, pressure
Bernoulli/efflux (range of a jet from a tank), viscosity and elastic energy problems
Polytropic process PVⁿ = const or P ∝ V: molar heat capacity and work; cyclic process on P–V diagrams
Heat conduction through composite rods in series/parallel; radiation (Stefan, Wien) comparisons
Time period of spring/rod/fluid systems and energy in SHM, including combinations of springs
Organ pipes and strings (harmonics, end correction) and Doppler effect with moving source/observer
Capacitor partly filled with dielectric slabs (side-by-side or stacked): capacitance, energy, charge redistribution
Gauss’s law for spheres/shells: field and potential inside and outside, ratios at given radii
RC charging/discharging: time for charge, current or energy to reach a fraction; meter/bridge circuits
Helical motion of a charge in B (pitch/radius), and Biot–Savart field of loops, polygons and finite segments
LR growth/decay (energy fraction vs time) and AC phasor problems with power factor
Silvered lens or lens–mirror combinations; refraction at spherical surfaces
YDSE with a thin film/slab shifting the pattern, intensity at a point, path difference
Radioactive decay laws: activity ratios, mean life, mixtures of two nuclides
Photoelectric effect: change of stopping potential/KE with wavelength; de Broglie relations
Redox titration stoichiometry with n-factors (KMnO₄ / K₂Cr₂O₇ against Fe²⁺ or oxalate)
Bohr energies/radii for H-like ions and number of spectral lines between levels
VSEPR: lone pairs, shapes and isostructural species among interhalogens, xenon compounds and ions
MOT: bond order, bond length order and magnetism of diatomic species and ions
Graham’s law effusion, van der Waals/compressibility factor reasoning
Reversible isothermal/adiabatic expansions: work, ΔS, ΔG; sign conventions
pH of salt hydrolysis, buffer (partial neutralisation) and weak acid solutions
Kp/Kc from degree of dissociation at total pressure P; Le Chatelier shifts
Kohlrausch law, combining standard potentials (via ΔG°), Nernst equation
Arrhenius from two temperatures; first-order half-life and fraction-completed relations
Raoult’s law vapour composition; colligative properties with association/dissociation (van’t Hoff factor)
Structures of oxoacids of P/S/Cl (P–H, P–OH, P–O–P counts) and products of p-block reactions
Ore concentration and extraction methods (froth flotation, self-reduction, electrolytic), s-block compound properties
Hybridisation, spin-only magnetic moment and isomerism of complexes (strong vs weak field)
KMnO₄/K₂Cr₂O₇ redox chemistry and transition-metal compound properties
Counting stereoisomers (chiral centres, meso forms, E/Z double bonds)
Counting structural isomers; acidity/basicity orders including heterocycles
Carbocation rearrangement in Friedel–Crafts alkylation or HX addition — major product
SN1/SN2 stereochemical outcome, ether cleavage with HI, phenol reactions
Aldol vs Cannizzaro feasibility (α-H), crossed Cannizzaro products, named-reaction sequences
Diazonium salt transformations (Sandmeyer, coupling) and amine reactions
Monomers of common polymers, biodegradable polymers, sugar/amino-acid structure facts
Counting functions with conditions (onto, one-one, no fixed points) between small finite sets
Number of solutions of equations mixing z, z̄ and powers (zⁿ = z̄, z̄ = z²); loci
Location of roots relative to numbers/intervals (discriminant, vertex, f(k) conditions)
Mixed AP/GP conditions and special sums (Σn(n+1), telescoping)
Integer solutions with upper bounds via inclusion–exclusion; distribution of identical objects
Remainders of large powers; sums like Σ r·C(n,r) using binomial identities
Cayley–Hamilton / matrix powers expressed as αA + βI; determinant properties
Counting matrices with entries from a small set satisfying a determinant/trace/symmetry condition
Dice/coin outcome counting for sums, products or patterns
Conditional probability/Bayes with urns chosen by a coin or die; maximum/minimum of repeated trials
Number of solutions of trigonometric equations in an interval, with domain restrictions (sec, tan undefined)
Common chords, common tangents and relative position of two circles
Parabola chords and normals: normal meeting again, chord subtending right angle at vertex
Ellipse/hyperbola focal properties, eccentricity and areas of focal triangles
Counting points of discontinuity/non-differentiability of GIF, modulus or max/min functions
Local extrema/monotonicity of polynomial or rational functions; minimum via AM–GM or derivative
Definite integrals of x·f(sin x) or similar using King’s property
Area of regions bounded by curves, lines and modulus functions
Homogeneous or linear DE with initial condition; value of the solution at a point
Scalar triple products, volumes and dot-product identities for vectors with given relations
Image/foot of a point in a plane, distances between planes, line–plane relations
Limit of a sum as a definite integral (Riemann sums)

resources.notes: Every organising IIT publishes both question papers (English and Hindi) and the provisional/final answer keys on jeeadv.ac.in; older years are in the site's archive section. An official mock CBT link is posted on jeeadv.ac.in before registration.

questions.question: A screw gauge has pitch 0.5 mm and 50 circular divisions. With the jaws closed it reads +0.03 mm. When a wire is held between the jaws, the main scale shows 3.0 mm and the circular scale division 26 coincides with the reference line. The corrected diameter of the wire is
questions.explanation: Least count = 0.5/50 = 0.01 mm. Observed = 3.0 + 26 × 0.01 = 3.26 mm. Positive zero error is subtracted: 3.26 − 0.03 = 3.23 mm.

questions.question: In a simple-pendulum experiment g = 4π²L/T². If L is measured with 1% error and T with 2% error, the maximum percentage error in g is
A projectile is launched from level ground at 20 m/s at 60° above the horizontal. After what time is its velocity perpendicular to its initial velocity? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: v·u = u² − gt·u sinθ = 0 ⇒ t = u/(g sinθ) = 20/(10 × √3/2) = 4/√3 ≈ 2.31 s, which is less than the flight time 2√3 s, so it occurs in flight.

questions.question: Block A (2 kg) rests on block B (4 kg), which lies on a frictionless floor. The coefficient of friction between A and B is 0.5. A horizontal force F is applied to B. The largest F for which the blocks move together is (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Friction can give A at most a = μg = 5 m/s². Moving together: F = (2 + 4) × 5 = 30 N.

questions.question: A ball of mass m moving with speed v collides head-on and elastically with a stationary ball of mass 2m. The fraction of the initial kinetic energy transferred to the heavier ball is
questions.explanation: Fraction transferred = 4m₁m₂/(m₁ + m₂)² = 4·m·2m/(3m)² = 8/9.

questions.question: A uniform disc of radius R spinning about its axis with angular speed ω₀ (centre at rest) is gently placed upright on its rim on a rough horizontal floor. When it starts pure rolling, the speed of its centre is
questions.explanation: Friction acts at the contact point, so angular momentum about that point is conserved: ½MR²ω₀ = ½MR²ω + MvR with v = ωR ⇒ ½ω₀ = (3/2)ω ⇒ ω = ω₀/3, v = ω₀R/3.

questions.question: A solid cylinder and a thin hollow cylinder of equal mass and radius roll without slipping from rest down the same incline from the same height. The ratio of their times of descent (t_solid : t_hollow) is
questions.explanation: a = g sinθ/(1 + k²/R²): solid 2g sinθ/3, hollow g sinθ/2. t ∝ 1/√a ⇒ t_s/t_h = √((1/2)/(2/3)) = √(3/4) = √3/2.

questions.question: A satellite moves in a circular orbit with speed v. The minimum additional speed it must be given (along its velocity) to escape the Earth's gravity is
questions.explanation: Escape speed at the orbit radius is √2 times the orbital speed, so the extra speed needed is √2v − v = (√2 − 1)v.

questions.question: Water rises to a height h in a capillary tube on the ground. If the same experiment is done in a lift accelerating upward at g/2, the height of rise becomes
questions.explanation: h = 2T cosθ/(rρg_eff). In the lift g_eff = g + g/2 = 3g/2, so h' = h/(3/2) = 2h/3.

questions.question: An ideal monatomic gas undergoes a process in which pressure is directly proportional to volume (P ∝ V). Its molar heat capacity for this process is
questions.explanation: P ∝ V means PV⁻¹ = constant, a polytropic process with n = −1. C = C_v − R/(n − 1) = 3R/2 + R/2 = 2R.

questions.question: Two rods of the same length and cross-section, with thermal conductivities K and 2K, are joined end to end. The effective thermal conductivity of the composite rod is
questions.explanation: Series thermal resistances: 2L/(K_eff A) = L/(KA) + L/(2KA) ⇒ K_eff = 2·K·2K/(K + 2K) = 4K/3.

questions.question: The fundamental frequency of a pipe closed at one end is 100 Hz. The second harmonic of an open pipe of the same length is
questions.explanation: Closed pipe: v/4L = 100 Hz ⇒ v/2L = 200 Hz is the open pipe's fundamental. Its second harmonic is 400 Hz.

questions.question: A parallel-plate capacitor of capacitance C₀ (air) has a dielectric slab of constant 4 inserted, filling the full plate area and half the gap thickness. The new capacitance is
A solid non-conducting sphere of radius R carries charge Q uniformly through its volume. The ratio of the electric field at distance R/2 from the centre to that at distance 2R is
questions.explanation: Inside: E = kQr/R³ = kQ/(2R²) at R/2. Outside: E = kQ/(4R²) at 2R. Ratio = 2 : 1.

questions.question: A capacitor is charged through a resistor from an ideal battery; the time constant is τ. The energy stored in the capacitor reaches half of its final value at time
A charged particle enters a uniform magnetic field with its velocity at 60° to the field. The ratio of the pitch of its helical path to the radius of the helix is
questions.explanation: Pitch = 2πm v cosθ/(qB); radius = m v sinθ/(qB). Ratio = 2π cot 60° = 2π/√3.

questions.question: In an L–R circuit connected to a battery at t = 0, the magnetic energy stored in the inductor reaches one-quarter of its final value at time (τ = L/R)
questions.explanation: U ∝ i², so U = U_f/4 when i = i₀/2: 1 − e^(−t/τ) = 1/2 ⇒ t = τ ln 2.

questions.question: A thin plano-convex lens (refractive index 1.5) has its curved surface of radius 20 cm. Its plane surface is silvered. The system behaves like a concave mirror of focal length
questions.explanation: Lens focal length f = R/(μ − 1) = 40 cm. Silvered plane face (P_m = 0): P = 2/f = 1/20 cm⁻¹, so F = 20 cm, equivalent to R/(2(μ − 1)).

questions.question: The activity of a radioactive sample falls to 1/16 of its initial value in 40 days. The mean life of the nuclide is approximately
questions.explanation: 1/16 = (1/2)⁴ ⇒ 4 half-lives = 40 days ⇒ T½ = 10 days. Mean life τ = T½/0.693 ≈ 14.4 days.

questions.question: When light of wavelength 400 nm falls on a metal, the stopping potential is V₀. If 300 nm light is used instead, the stopping potential increases by approximately (hc = 1240 eV nm)
questions.explanation: ΔV = (hc/e)(1/300 − 1/400) = 1240 × (1/1200) ≈ 1.03 V; the work function cancels.

questions.question: What volume of 0.1 M KMnO₄ is needed to oxidise 50 mL of 0.5 M FeSO₄ in acidic medium?
questions.explanation: MnO₄⁻ + 5Fe²⁺ + 8H⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 5Fe³⁺ + 4H₂O. Fe²⁺ = 25 mmol needs 5 mmol MnO₄⁻ = 50 mL of 0.1 M.

questions.question: According to Bohr's model, the energy of the electron in the third orbit of Li²⁺ is
Which of the following has the largest number of lone pairs on the central atom?
questions.explanation: Lone pairs on central atom: XeF₂ = 3, ClF₃ = 2, IF₅ = 1, SF₄ = 1.

questions.question: Which pair of species is isostructural?
questions.explanation: XeF₄ and ICl₄⁻ both have 4 bond pairs + 2 lone pairs and are square planar. SF₄ is see-saw, NH₃ pyramidal vs BF₃ planar, SO₃²⁻ pyramidal vs SO₃ planar.

questions.question: Two moles of an ideal gas expand isothermally and reversibly at 300 K from 10 L to 100 L. The work done on the gas is (R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)
The pH of a 0.1 M aqueous solution of sodium acetate is (pKa of acetic acid = 4.74, 25 °C)
questions.explanation: Salt of weak acid and strong base: pH = 7 + ½(pKa + log C) = 7 + ½(4.74 − 1) = 8.87.

questions.question: N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g) is 20% dissociated at equilibrium at a total pressure of 1 atm. Kp for the reaction is approximately
questions.explanation: Mole fractions: NO₂ = 2α/(1 + α), N₂O₄ = (1 − α)/(1 + α). Kp = 4α²P/(1 − α²) = 4(0.04)(1)/0.96 ≈ 0.167 atm.

questions.question: Given Λ°m (S cm² mol⁻¹): HCl = 426, NaCl = 126, CH₃COONa = 91. Λ°m of CH₃COOH is
questions.explanation: By Kohlrausch's law: Λ°(CH₃COOH) = Λ°(CH₃COONa) + Λ°(HCl) − Λ°(NaCl) = 91 + 426 − 126 = 391.

questions.question: The rate constant of a reaction doubles when the temperature rises from 300 K to 310 K. The activation energy is approximately (R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)
An ideal solution contains 1 mol of A (P°A = 100 torr) and 3 mol of B (P°B = 60 torr). The mole fraction of A in the vapour in equilibrium is
Which oxoacid of phosphorus contains two P–H bonds?
questions.explanation: Hypophosphorous acid H₃PO₂ has one P–OH, one P=O and two P–H bonds (monobasic). H₃PO₃ has one P–H; H₃PO₄ and H₄P₂O₇ have none.

questions.question: Which ore is usually concentrated by froth flotation?
questions.explanation: Froth flotation is used for sulphide ores; galena is PbS. Haematite and cassiterite are oxides (gravity/magnetic methods) and bauxite is leached.

questions.question: Which complex is an inner-orbital (d²sp³) complex and diamagnetic?
questions.explanation: Co³⁺ (d⁶) with NH₃ is low spin: all six electrons paired in t₂g, d²sp³ hybridised. [CoF₆]³⁻ and [Fe(H₂O)₆]²⁺ are high spin; [MnCl₄]²⁻ is sp³ with 5 unpaired electrons.

questions.question: The total number of stereoisomers of 2,3-dibromobutane is
questions.explanation: Two stereocentres with identical substitution: (2R,3R), (2S,3S) enantiomers and one meso form = 3.

questions.question: The number of structurally isomeric alcohols with the molecular formula C₅H₁₂O is
questions.explanation: Pentan-1-ol, pentan-2-ol, pentan-3-ol, 2-methylbutan-1-ol, 2-methylbutan-2-ol, 3-methylbutan-2-ol, 3-methylbutan-1-ol and 2,2-dimethylpropan-1-ol = 8.

questions.question: Benzene reacts with 1-chloro-2-methylpropane, (CH₃)₂CHCH₂Cl, in the presence of anhydrous AlCl₃. The major product is
questions.explanation: The primary carbocation (or its AlCl₃ complex) rearranges by a 1,2-hydride shift to the tertiary (CH₃)₃C⁺, which alkylates benzene to give tert-butylbenzene.

questions.question: (R)-2-Bromobutane reacts with aqueous NaOH by an SN2 mechanism. The product is
questions.explanation: SN2 proceeds with backside attack and Walden inversion. OH replaces Br with the same priority ranking, so R becomes S.

questions.question: Which of the following cannot undergo aldol condensation?
questions.explanation: Aldol condensation needs an α-hydrogen. (CH₃)₃C–CHO has no α-H (it undergoes Cannizzaro reaction instead).

questions.question: Aniline is diazotised with NaNO₂/HCl at 0–5 °C and the product is treated with CuCN/KCN. The final product is
questions.explanation: Sandmeyer reaction: C₆H₅N₂⁺Cl⁻ + CuCN → C₆H₅CN (benzonitrile) + N₂.

questions.question: Nylon-6,6 is obtained by condensation polymerisation of
questions.explanation: Nylon-6,6 is the polyamide of H₂N(CH₂)₆NH₂ and HOOC(CH₂)₄COOH; caprolactam gives nylon-6, glycol + terephthalic acid gives PET, phenol + HCHO gives bakelite.

questions.question: The number of onto functions from a set with 4 elements to a set with 3 elements is
questions.explanation: By inclusion–exclusion: 3⁴ − C(3,1)2⁴ + C(3,2)1⁴ = 81 − 48 + 3 = 36.

questions.question: The number of complex numbers z satisfying z̄ = z² is
questions.explanation: Taking moduli: |z| = |z|² ⇒ |z| = 0 or 1. z = 0 works. If |z| = 1, z̄ = 1/z so z³ = 1, giving three roots. Total 4.

questions.question: Both roots of x² − 2kx + k² − 1 = 0 lie in the interval (−2, 4) if and only if k belongs to
questions.explanation: The roots are k − 1 and k + 1. Need k − 1 > −2 and k + 1 < 4 ⇒ −1 < k < 3.

questions.question: a, b, c are in a non-constant geometric progression and a, 2b, 3c are in arithmetic progression. The common ratio of the GP is
questions.explanation: 4b = a + 3c ⇒ 4ar = a + 3ar² ⇒ 3r² − 4r + 1 = 0 ⇒ r = 1 or 1/3. Non-constant ⇒ r = 1/3.

questions.question: The number of non-negative integer solutions of x + y + z = 10 with each of x, y, z at most 5 is
questions.explanation: Total = C(12, 2) = 66. Solutions with x ≥ 6: x' + y + z = 4 ⇒ C(6, 2) = 15; times 3 variables = 45 (two variables ≥ 6 impossible). 66 − 45 = 21.

questions.question: The remainder when 7¹⁰³ is divided by 25 is
For A = [[1, 2], [3, 4]] (rows), A² = αA + βI. Then (α, β) equals
questions.explanation: Characteristic equation: λ² − (tr A)λ + det A = λ² − 5λ − 2 = 0. By Cayley–Hamilton, A² = 5A + 2I.

questions.question: Three fair dice are thrown. The probability that the sum of the numbers shown is 10 is
questions.explanation: Number of ordered triples (1–6) with sum 10 is 27 (coefficient of x¹⁰ in (x + … + x⁶)³). Probability = 27/216 = 1/8.

questions.question: A fair die is rolled 4 times. The probability that the largest number obtained is exactly 4 is
The number of solutions of sin 2x = cos x in the interval [0, 2π] is
questions.explanation: cos x(2 sin x − 1) = 0 ⇒ cos x = 0 (x = π/2, 3π/2) or sin x = 1/2 (x = π/6, 5π/6). Total 4.

questions.question: The length of the common chord of the circles x² + y² = 16 and (x − 6)² + y² = 16 is
questions.explanation: Subtracting gives the chord x = 3. Half-length = √(16 − 9) = √7, so the chord is 2√7.

questions.question: The normal to the parabola y² = 4x at the point (1, 2) meets the parabola again at
questions.explanation: (1, 2) is (at², 2at) with a = 1, t = 1. The normal at t meets the parabola again at t₂ = −t − 2/t = −3, i.e. (9, −6).

questions.question: The equation of the hyperbola (axes along the coordinate axes) with eccentricity 2 and distance between foci 16 is
The number of points in the open interval (0, 3) at which f(x) = [x²] is discontinuous ([·] = greatest integer function) is
questions.explanation: x² runs over (0, 9) and [x²] jumps whenever x² is an integer 1, 2, …, 8, i.e. at x = 1, √2, √3, 2, √5, √6, √7, √8: 8 points.

questions.question: The minimum value of f(x) = x² + 16/x for x > 0 is
The value of ∫ from 0 to π of x sin x/(1 + cos²x) dx is
questions.explanation: Using x → π − x: I = (π/2)∫₀^π sin x/(1 + cos²x) dx = (π/2)[−tan⁻¹(cos x)]₀^π = (π/2)(π/4 + π/4) = π²/4.

questions.question: The area of the region enclosed by y = |x| and y = 2 − x² is
questions.explanation: For x ≥ 0 the curves meet at x = 1. Area = 2∫₀¹ (2 − x² − x) dx = 2(2 − 1/3 − 1/2) = 7/3.

questions.question: The general solution of dy/dx = y/x + tan(y/x) is
questions.explanation: Put y = vx: x dv/dx = tan v ⇒ cot v dv = dx/x ⇒ ln sin v = ln x + c ⇒ sin(y/x) = Cx.

questions.question: If [a b c] = 4, the volume of the parallelepiped with coterminous edges a + b, b + c and c + a is
questions.explanation: [a+b  b+c  c+a] = 2[a b c] = 8.

questions.question: The image of the point (1, 2, 3) in the plane x + y + z = 0 is

A vernier calliper has a least count of 0.01 cm and a zero error of −0.04 cm. While measuring the length of a rod, the main-scale reading is 3.2 cm and the 6th vernier division coincides with a main-scale division. The corrected length of the rod is
questions.explanation: Observed reading = 3.2 + 6 × 0.01 = 3.26 cm. Corrected = observed − (zero error) = 3.26 − (−0.04) = 3.30 cm.

questions.question: A length l is formed as l = hᵃ cᵇ Gᶜ from Planck’s constant h, the speed of light c and the gravitational constant G. Then (a, b, c) is
questions.explanation: [h] = ML²T⁻¹, [c] = LT⁻¹, [G] = M⁻¹L³T⁻². M: a − c = 0; T: −a − b − 2c = 0; L: 2a + b + 3c = 1. With c = a: b = −3a and 2a − 3a + 3a = 1 ⇒ a = 1/2, b = −3/2, c = 1/2, i.e. l = √(hG/c³).

questions.question: A river 400 m wide flows at 3 m/s. A boat that moves at 5 m/s relative to the water is steered so that it crosses along the shortest path, reaching the point directly opposite. The time taken to cross is
questions.explanation: To move straight across, the upstream component of the boat’s velocity must cancel the river flow: v_across = √(5² − 3²) = 4 m/s. t = 400/4 = 100 s. (80 s is the minimum-time crossing, which drifts downstream.)

questions.question: Block A (3 kg) rests on block B (2 kg), which lies on a frictionless horizontal floor. The coefficient of static friction between A and B is 0.4. A horizontal force F is applied to A. The maximum F for which the blocks move together is (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: B is driven only by friction: its maximum acceleration is μm_Ag/m_B = 0.4 × 30/2 = 6 m/s². Moving together, F = (3 + 2) × 6 = 30 N. (12 N is just the limiting friction.)

questions.question: A ball is dropped from a height of 5 m onto a horizontal floor. The coefficient of restitution is 0.5. The total distance travelled by the ball before it comes to rest is
questions.explanation: Successive rebound heights are he², he⁴, … Total distance = h + 2h(e² + e⁴ + …) = h(1 + e²)/(1 − e²) = 5 × 1.25/0.75 = 25/3 m.

questions.question: A thin ring of radius R spinning about its axis with angular speed ω₀ (centre at rest) is gently placed upright on a rough horizontal floor. The linear speed of its centre when pure rolling begins is
questions.explanation: Friction acts at the contact point, so angular momentum about it is conserved: mR²ω₀ = (mR² + mR²)ω ⇒ ω = ω₀/2, v = ω₀R/2. (ω₀R/3 is the answer for a disc.)

questions.question: A uniform solid sphere rolls down a rough incline of angle θ without slipping. The minimum coefficient of static friction required is
questions.explanation: For rolling, a = g sin θ/(1 + k²/R²) = (5/7)g sin θ and f = m g sin θ − ma = (2/7)mg sin θ ≤ μ mg cos θ ⇒ μ ≥ (2/7) tan θ.

questions.question: Two satellites move in circular orbits at heights R and 3R above the Earth’s surface (R = radius of the Earth). The ratio of their time periods T₁ : T₂ is
questions.explanation: Orbit radii are 2R and 4R. T ∝ r^(3/2): T₁/T₂ = (1/2)^(3/2) = 1/(2√2). (Using heights instead of radii gives a wrong ratio.)

questions.question: A wooden block floats in water in a container with 3/5 of its volume submerged. The container is now placed in a lift accelerating upward at g/2. The fraction of the block’s volume now submerged is
questions.explanation: Both the weight and the buoyant force scale with the effective gravity g + a, so the floating condition ρ_b V = ρ_w V_sub is unchanged: still 3/5.

questions.question: Two radioactive samples A (half-life 2 h) and B (half-life 4 h) initially contain equal numbers of nuclei. After 8 h, the ratio N_A : N_B of undecayed nuclei is
questions.explanation: After 8 h, A has gone through 4 half-lives (1/16 left) and B through 2 (1/4 left). Ratio = (1/16)/(1/4) = 1/4.

questions.question: One mole of an ideal diatomic gas undergoes a process in which PV² = constant. The molar heat capacity of the gas in this process is
questions.explanation: For PVⁿ = const, C = Cv + R/(1 − n). With Cv = 5R/2 and n = 2: C = 5R/2 − R = 3R/2.

questions.question: Two rods of the same length are placed in parallel between two heat reservoirs. One has conductivity K and cross-sectional area A, the other has conductivity 3K and area 2A. The effective conductivity of the combination (total area 3A) is
questions.explanation: In parallel the thermal conductances add: K_eq(3A)/L = KA/L + 3K(2A)/L = 7KA/L ⇒ K_eq = 7K/3.

questions.question: In a Young’s double-slit experiment with light of wavelength 600 nm, a thin transparent film of refractive index 1.5 placed over one slit shifts the central bright fringe by 5 fringe widths. The thickness of the film is
questions.explanation: Extra optical path (μ − 1)t = nλ ⇒ t = 5 × 600 nm/0.5 = 6000 nm = 6 μm.

questions.question: A source of sound of frequency f moves directly towards a stationary observer with speed v/10, where v is the speed of sound. The frequency heard by the observer is
questions.explanation: f′ = f v/(v − v_s) = f v/(v − v/10) = 10f/9. (11f/10 is the result for an observer moving at v/10 towards a stationary source.)

questions.question: A parallel-plate capacitor has capacitance C₀ with air. Over the left half of the plate area, a slab of dielectric constant 3 fills the whole gap; over the right half, a slab of dielectric constant 3 fills half the gap thickness (the rest is air). The new capacitance is
questions.explanation: Left half: 3 × C₀/2 = 3C₀/2. Right half: air and dielectric in series, C = (C₀/2) × 2K/(K + 1) = (C₀/2)(6/4) = 3C₀/4. The halves are in parallel: 3C₀/2 + 3C₀/4 = 9C₀/4.

questions.question: A thin spherical shell of radius R carries charge Q, and a point charge q is placed at its centre. With k = 1/(4πε₀), the potential at a distance R/2 from the centre is
questions.explanation: Inside the shell its potential is constant at kQ/R; the point charge contributes kq/(R/2) = 2kq/R. Total = k(2q + Q)/R.

questions.question: A capacitor of capacitance C charged to a potential V₀ is discharged through a resistor R. The time after which the energy stored becomes one-fourth of its initial value is
questions.explanation: q = q₀e^(−t/RC), so U ∝ q² ∝ e^(−2t/RC). e^(−2t/RC) = 1/4 ⇒ 2t/RC = ln 4 = 2 ln 2 ⇒ t = RC ln 2.

questions.question: A wire bent into a square of side a carries a current I. The magnitude of the magnetic field at the centre of the square is
questions.explanation: Each side (distance a/2, subtending 45° on each side): B = (μ₀I/(4π · a/2))(sin 45° + sin 45°) = √2μ₀I/(2πa). Four sides add: 4 × √2μ₀I/(2πa) = 2√2 μ₀I/(πa).

questions.question: A series combination of a resistor R and an inductor with X_L = √3 R is connected to an AC source of fixed rms voltage and frequency. A capacitor is then added in series so that the power factor becomes 1. The ratio of the new average power to the original average power is
questions.explanation: Originally Z = √(R² + 3R²) = 2R and P = V²R/Z² = V²/(4R). At unity power factor Z = R and P = V²/R. Ratio = 4.

questions.question: Light of wavelength λ ejects photoelectrons with maximum kinetic energy K from a metal of work function φ. If light of wavelength λ/2 is used instead, the maximum kinetic energy becomes
questions.explanation: hc/λ = K + φ. For λ/2: K′ = 2hc/λ − φ = 2(K + φ) − φ = 2K + φ.

questions.question: The volume of 0.02 M K₂Cr₂O₇ solution required to oxidise 30 mL of 0.1 M FeSO₄ completely in acidic medium is
questions.explanation: Milliequivalents of Fe²⁺ = 30 × 0.1 × 1 = 3. Dichromate n-factor = 6: 0.02 × 6 × V = 3 ⇒ V = 25 mL. (150 mL results from ignoring the n-factor of dichromate.)

questions.question: Which of the following is a biodegradable polymer?
questions.explanation: PHBV (poly-β-hydroxybutyrate-co-β-hydroxyvalerate) is an aliphatic polyester degraded by bacteria. Nylon-6, PVC and Bakelite are non-biodegradable.

questions.question: The correct order of increasing bond length is
questions.explanation: Bond orders: O₂⁺ 2.5, O₂ 2, O₂⁻ 1.5, O₂²⁻ 1. Bond length increases as bond order decreases.

questions.question: Under identical conditions of temperature and pressure, an unknown gas effuses at half the rate of oxygen. The molar mass of the gas is
questions.explanation: Graham’s law: r₁/r₂ = √(M₂/M₁) ⇒ 1/2 = √(32/M) ⇒ M = 128 g mol⁻¹. (64 results from forgetting the square root.)

questions.question: One mole of an ideal gas expands isothermally and reversibly at 300 K from 2 L to 20 L. The entropy change of the gas is approximately (R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)
questions.explanation: ΔS = nR ln(V₂/V₁) = 8.314 × 2.303 × log 10 ≈ 19.1 J K⁻¹. The surroundings change by −19.1 J K⁻¹, so only the total is zero.

questions.question: 0.2 mol of acetic acid and 0.1 mol of NaOH are dissolved in water to make 1 L of solution. The pH of the solution is (pKa of acetic acid = 4.74)
questions.explanation: NaOH neutralises 0.1 mol acid, leaving 0.1 mol CH₃COOH and 0.1 mol CH₃COO⁻. Henderson: pH = 4.74 + log(0.1/0.1) = 4.74.

questions.question: PCl₅(g) ⇌ PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g). Starting from pure PCl₅, the degree of dissociation at equilibrium is α at a total pressure P. Kp is
questions.explanation: Moles: PCl₅ 1 − α, PCl₃ α, Cl₂ α; total 1 + α. Kp = [(α/(1 + α))P]²/[((1 − α)/(1 + α))P] = α²P/(1 − α²).

questions.question: Given E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V and E°(Cu⁺/Cu) = +0.52 V, the value of E°(Cu²⁺/Cu⁺) is
questions.explanation: Add free energies, not potentials: −2F(0.34) = −1F(E) − 1F(0.52) ⇒ E = 0.68 − 0.52 = 0.16 V. (0.18 V comes from simply subtracting the potentials.)

questions.question: A first-order reaction is 75% complete in 60 minutes. The time required for 87.5% completion is
questions.explanation: 75% completion = 2 half-lives ⇒ t½ = 30 min. 87.5% completion = 3 half-lives = 90 min.

questions.question: A solution of benzoic acid in benzene shows a freezing-point depression of 0.64 K for 2.44 g of acid (M = 122 g mol⁻¹) in 100 g of benzene (Kf = 5.12 K kg mol⁻¹). The percentage of benzoic acid that is dimerised is
The numbers of P–OH bonds in hypophosphorous acid (H₃PO₂), phosphorous acid (H₃PO₃) and pyrophosphoric acid (H₄P₂O₇) are respectively
questions.explanation: H₃PO₂ has two P–H and one P–OH; H₃PO₃ has one P–H and two P–OH; H₄P₂O₇ has four P–OH (all H ionisable).

questions.question: Which metal is extracted from its sulphide ore by self-reduction (auto-reduction) after partial roasting?
questions.explanation: Cu₂S partly oxidised to Cu₂O reacts with remaining Cu₂S: 2Cu₂O + Cu₂S → 6Cu + SO₂. ZnO is reduced by coke, Al is obtained electrolytically, Fe by coke in a blast furnace.

questions.question: The spin-only magnetic moments of [Fe(H₂O)₆]³⁺ and [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻ are respectively
questions.explanation: Fe³⁺ is d⁵. H₂O (weak field) gives high spin with 5 unpaired electrons: √35 ≈ 5.92 BM. CN⁻ (strong field) gives t₂g⁵ with 1 unpaired electron: √3 ≈ 1.73 BM.

questions.question: The number of moles of KMnO₄ that react with one mole of oxalate ions (C₂O₄²⁻) in acidic medium is
questions.explanation: MnO₄⁻ gains 5e⁻; C₂O₄²⁻ loses 2e⁻ (→ 2CO₂). Moles MnO₄⁻ × 5 = 1 × 2 ⇒ 0.4 mol (2MnO₄⁻ : 5C₂O₄²⁻).

questions.question: The total number of stereoisomers possible for pent-3-en-2-ol, CH₃–CH=CH–CH(OH)–CH₃, is
questions.explanation: There is one chiral carbon (C-2) and one double bond capable of E/Z isomerism; the two are independent, so 2 × 2 = 4 stereoisomers.

questions.question: The correct order of basic strength of piperidine, pyridine and pyrrole is
questions.explanation: Piperidine has an sp³ nitrogen lone pair; pyridine’s lone pair is sp² (more s-character, less available); in pyrrole the lone pair is part of the aromatic sextet, so it is barely basic.

questions.question: 3-Methylbut-1-ene reacts with HBr in the absence of peroxide. The major product is
questions.explanation: Protonation gives a 2° carbocation at C-2, which undergoes a 1,2-hydride shift to the more stable 3° carbocation at C-3; bromide attack there gives 2-bromo-2-methylbutane.

questions.question: Anisole (methoxybenzene) is heated with concentrated HI. The products are
questions.explanation: The protonated ether is attacked by I⁻ at the methyl carbon (SN2); the aryl C–O bond has partial double-bond character and is not cleaved. Products: C₆H₅OH + CH₃I.

questions.question: A mixture of formaldehyde and benzaldehyde is heated with concentrated NaOH (crossed Cannizzaro reaction). The main products are
questions.explanation: Formaldehyde is the most reactive towards OH⁻ and is preferentially oxidised to formate, transferring hydride to benzaldehyde, which is reduced to benzyl alcohol.

questions.question: Benzenediazonium chloride is treated with phenol in mildly alkaline solution. The product is
questions.explanation: The diazonium ion acts as an electrophile and couples with phenoxide at the para position, giving the orange azo dye p-hydroxyazobenzene.

questions.question: The number of functions f : {1, 2, 3, 4} → {1, 2, 3, 4} that are one-one and satisfy f(i) ≠ i for every i is
questions.explanation: These are derangements of 4 objects: D₄ = 4!(1 − 1 + 1/2 − 1/6 + 1/24) = 12 − 4 + 1 = 9.

questions.question: The number of complex numbers z satisfying z⁴ = z̄ is
questions.explanation: Taking moduli, |z|⁴ = |z| ⇒ |z| = 0 or 1. z = 0 works. If |z| = 1, z̄ = 1/z so z⁵ = 1, giving 5 roots. Total 6.

questions.question: Both roots of x² − 2kx + 4 = 0 are real and greater than 1 if and only if k lies in
questions.explanation: Real roots: 4k² − 16 ≥ 0 ⇒ |k| ≥ 2. Vertex k > 1. f(1) = 5 − 2k > 0 ⇒ k < 5/2. Together k ∈ [2, 5/2) (k = 2 gives the double root 2).

questions.question: The distance between the parallel planes 2x − y + 2z = 3 and 4x − 2y + 4z = 15 is
questions.explanation: Rewrite the second plane as 2x − y + 2z = 7.5. Distance = |7.5 − 3|/√(4 + 1 + 4) = 4.5/3 = 3/2. (4 comes from not rescaling the second equation.)

questions.question: The number of ways of distributing 8 identical balls into 3 distinct boxes so that no box contains more than 4 balls is
questions.explanation: Without the cap: C(10,2) = 45. Solutions with some box ≥ 5: put 5 in it and distribute 3: C(5,2) = 10 for each of 3 boxes = 30 (two boxes cannot both exceed 4). 45 − 30 = 15.

questions.question: If a, b and c are unit vectors with a + b + c = 0, then a·b + b·c + c·a equals
questions.explanation: |a + b + c|² = 3 + 2(a·b + b·c + c·a) = 0 ⇒ the sum is −3/2.

questions.question: For A = [[2, −1], [1, 0]] (rows), A³ equals
questions.explanation: Characteristic equation λ² − 2λ + 1 = 0 ⇒ A² = 2A − I (Cayley–Hamilton). A³ = 2A² − A = 2(2A − I) − A = 3A − 2I.

questions.question: The number of 2 × 2 matrices with every entry from {0, 1} whose determinant is zero is
questions.explanation: det = ad − bc with ad, bc ∈ {0, 1}. det = 0 when ad = bc = 0 (3 × 3 = 9 ways) or ad = bc = 1 (1 way). Total 10.

questions.question: Two fair dice are thrown. The probability that the product of the numbers shown is a perfect square is
questions.explanation: Favourable: the 6 doubles plus (1, 4) and (4, 1) — 8 outcomes. 8/36 = 2/9.

questions.question: Box I contains 2 white and 3 black balls; Box II contains 4 white and 1 black ball. A fair coin is tossed: on heads Box I is chosen, on tails Box II. Two balls drawn together from the chosen box are both white. The probability that Box II was chosen is
The number of solutions of tan x + sec x = 2 cos x in the interval [0, 2π] is
questions.explanation: Multiply by cos x (≠ 0): sin x + 1 = 2cos²x = 2 − 2sin²x ⇒ 2sin²x + sin x − 1 = 0 ⇒ sin x = 1/2 or −1. sin x = −1 makes cos x = 0 (inadmissible). sin x = 1/2 gives π/6, 5π/6: 2 solutions.

questions.question: The number of common tangents to the circles x² + y² = 4 and x² + y² − 6x − 8y + 16 = 0 is
questions.explanation: Centres (0, 0) and (3, 4), radii 2 and √(9 + 16 − 16) = 3. Distance between centres = 5 = 2 + 3, so the circles touch externally: 3 common tangents.

questions.question: Every chord of the parabola y² = 4ax that subtends a right angle at the vertex passes through the fixed point
questions.explanation: For chord joining (at₁², 2at₁) and (at₂², 2at₂), perpendicularity at the vertex gives t₁t₂ = −4. The chord 2x − (t₁ + t₂)y + 2at₁t₂ = 0 then becomes 2x − (t₁ + t₂)y − 8a = 0, which passes through (4a, 0).

questions.question: P is a point on the ellipse x²/25 + y²/9 = 1 and S, S′ are its foci. The maximum area of triangle PSS′ is
questions.explanation: c = √(25 − 9) = 4, so SS′ = 8. Area = ½ × 8 × |y_P| is maximum when |y_P| = b = 3: area = 12.

questions.question: The number of points at which f(x) = |x² − 1| + |x − 2| is not differentiable is
questions.explanation: |x² − 1| has corners at x = ±1 (simple roots) and |x − 2| at x = 2; none cancel, so there are 3 points.

questions.question: The local maximum value of f(x) = x⁴ − 4x³ + 4x² is
questions.explanation: f′(x) = 4x(x − 1)(x − 2). f′ changes from + to − at x = 1, so f has a local maximum f(1) = 1 − 4 + 4 = 1 (local minima at 0 and 2 with value 0).

questions.question: The value of ∫ from 0 to π of x/(1 + sin x) dx is
questions.explanation: King’s property gives I = (π/2)∫₀^π dx/(1 + sin x). Since ∫ dx/(1 + sin x) = tan x − sec x, the integral from 0 to π equals 1 − (−1) = 2. So I = π.

questions.question: The area of the region bounded by y = √x, the line x + y = 2 and the x-axis is
questions.explanation: The curves meet at (1, 1). Area = ∫₀¹ √x dx + ∫₁² (2 − x) dx = 2/3 + 1/2 = 7/6.

questions.question: If y = y(x) satisfies x dy/dx = x + y with y(1) = 0, then y(e) equals
questions.explanation: dy/dx − y/x = 1; integrating factor 1/x: d(y/x)/dx = 1/x ⇒ y/x = ln x + C. y(1) = 0 ⇒ C = 0, so y = x ln x and y(e) = e.

questions.question: The value of lim (n → ∞) Σ (r = 1 to n) n/(n² + r²) is
